title: Circular Motion – I: Kinematics & Horizontal Plane
note: Take g = 10 m/s² unless stated otherwise.

subtopics.name: Horizontal Circle: Centripetal Force & Rotating Frames

questions.question: A car is moving in a circular path of radius R with a uniform speed v. Find magnitude of change in velocity and average acceleration when the car’s direction changes by θ.
A particle moves so that its position vector is given by $\overrightarrow{r} = \cos \omega t\widehat{x} + \sin \omega t\widehat{y}$. Where ω is a constant. Which of the following is true?

options.A: Velocity and acceleration both are perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{r}$.
options.B: Velocity and acceleration both are parallel to $\overrightarrow{r}$
options.C: Velocity is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{r}$ and acceleration is directed towards the origin
options.D: Velocity is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{r}$ and acceleration is directed away from the origin

questions.question: The position vector of a particle $\overrightarrow{R}\ $as a function of time is given by $\overrightarrow{R} = 4\sin(2\pi t)\widehat{i} + 4\cos(2\pi t)\widehat{j}$; where R is in meters, t is in seconds and $\widehat{i}\ $and $\widehat{j}$ denote unit vectors along x and y-directions, respectively. Which one of the following statements is wrong for the motion of particle ?

options.A: Path of the particle is a circle of radius 4 meter
options.C: Magnitude of acceleration vector is $\frac{v^{2}}{R}\ $where v is the velocity of particle.
options.D: Magnitude of the velocity of particle is 8 meter/second
